Practical

PRAK-tih-kuhl · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Practical is useful and sensible; likely to work well in real life.

Sneakers are more practical than sandals for the playground.

Worked Example

Keeping a spare pencil in your desk is a practical idea.

A spare pencil solves a real problem - a broken point in the middle of class. An idea that works well in real life is practical.

How Practical Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

useful

useful: helping to get things done

sensible

sensible: showing good sense

Antonyms

impractical

impractical: not workable in real life

useless

useless: giving no help at all

How Strong Is It? — Handy → practical → Necessary

Handy vs. practical

Handy vs. practical: Handy is milder: a hook by the door is handy for hanging your coat.

Necessary vs. practical

Necessary vs. practical: Necessary is stronger: in a rainstorm, boots are not just practical - they are necessary.

Put it together: Practic- means fit for action, so practical describes things that work well when you actually use them.
